body: PTAL. HTML now defines a document's `text-scale keyword`, and CSS uses it to determine the `text scale factor`.

AI review Reviewed at 07b4f41, together with the CSS companion davidsgrogan/csswg-drafts#1. Lint passes. The algorithm matches Chromium's `Document::TextScaleMetaChanged()`: it uses the first `meta[name=text-scale]` in tree order, compares case-insensitively, doesn't strip whitespace, and an invalid first element gives `legacy` without trying later elements. **Suggestions** - `source:18241-18242`: "matches one of the text-scale keywords" leaves case-sensitivity unclear, but the algorithm and CSS Fonts 5 use ASCII case-insensitive matching. Consider "is an ASCII case-insensitive match for one of the text-scale keywords". - `source:18238-18242`: unlike `color-scheme` and `theme-color`, the `
` never says what the name does. It opens straight with a conformance requirement. Consider a lead sentence, e.g. "A `text-scale` value indicates whether the page wants the text scale factor to include the user's OS-level text scale preference. CSSFONTS5" - `source:18282-18286`: *text-scale keyword* is now a value CSS pulls on demand ("CSS uses it to determine the text scale factor"). So "user agents must re-run the above algorithm" has no effect, because nothing consumes the re-run result. Either drop the paragraph, or say what has to be updated (e.g. the document's text scale factor), as `theme-color` does with "apply the result to any affected UI". - `source:18270-18276`: it returns the string `"legacy"` in two places and "that keyword" in another, while CSS compares against `[=text-scale/legacy=]` and `[=text-scale/scale=]`. Consider adding `legacy` and `scale` to Dependencies (`css-fonts-5/#text-scale-legacy`, `#text-scale-scale`) and returning them by reference, or returning the ASCII lowercase of the content value. **Nits** - `source:18259`: other per-document exports use `` (e.g. `source:11801`). Consider adding `for="Document"`, and `for: Document` to the CSS anchors block (in the CSS spec) to match. - `source:3964-3967`: the HTML term "text-scale keywords" (allowed values) and "text-scale keyword" (computed result) differ only by the plural, and the CSS anchor is a section heading (`

Keywords

`), not a dfn. Maybe rename the dependency to something like "recognized text-scale keywords" to keep the two apart. - PR body: the top of the description is meant to be the commit message, and "This spec text mostly references CSS. The color-scheme entry was used as a template." is process detail. Consider trimming it to the first sentence plus `Fixes #12526`.
